transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Uh... hi. I guess I'm here because... I just can't keep my words in a straight line anymore. Like, I'll start talking about my overnight shift, and... I don't know, I end up jumping to soccer, or paint colors, or the patient charts. I can see everyone getting lost when I talk. So... yeah. That's why.
Have you been feeling unusually energized, or perhaps exceptionally low or sad, at the same time that you've been having these difficulties with your speech?

Uh... no, not energized. Just... really low. Depressed, I guess. It's... when that gets to be at its worst, that's usually when... well, I'm sure the supervisors at work are watching me through the cameras. And... my words just get so tangled up then. I can't even explain myself clearly when it happens. So... yeah.
Do you find that these thoughts about being watched happen even when you aren't feeling particularly depressed?

Yeah... I guess so. There was... maybe a few weeks, a little while back, where I wasn't in that really deep, dark place. But... I still knew they were watching me. The supervisors, on the cameras. I just... had to be really careful at work. Keep my guard up. So... yeah.
Have you ever heard voices or sounds that other people around you cannot hear?
Uh... no. I don't... I haven't heard anything like that. Just... no.
How long have you been experiencing these difficulties with your speech and these concerns about being watched by your supervisors?

Uh... it's been a while, I guess. Maybe... around a year? And... a month, something like that. That's when I first noticed the cameras and... when talking started getting hard. So... yeah, about that long.
Aside from your speech difficulties, have you found it increasingly difficult to keep up with your daily hygiene, household chores, or social interactions with friends and family over this past year?

Yeah... things have slipped. Work is hard. I... I have to get the other aides to double-check my rounds. And my charting. Just to be sure. 

At home... I don't really talk to anyone. Bills are piling up. The apartment is a mess. I just... I can't. 

It got really bad recently. Employee health... they sent me here. For an emergency eval. Because... I told them I was thinking about ending it. So... yeah. Everything's just... hard.
Are there times during this past year when your speech becomes tangled and hard to follow, even when you aren't feeling depressed?

Yeah... I guess so. There was... maybe a few weeks. I wasn't feeling as down, you know? Not in that... that dark place. But... the cameras were still there. I still knew they were watching me. I had to be careful at work. Guarded. So... yeah. Even then.

Looking back over the entire year, were there any periods of at least two weeks where you experienced these thoughts about being watched by your supervisors while you were not feeling depressed at all?

I mean... like I just said. Yeah. There was a stretch of... a few weeks. I wasn't in that deep depressed place then. But... I still knew they were monitoring me. I still had to act really guarded on the floor. So... yes.
Looking back over the entire year, would you say that you have spent more of that time feeling depressed than you have spent feeling like your mood was relatively normal?

Yeah... I guess so. It's just... heavy. Empty. Most of the year, really. Even when the... the camera stuff was quieter... or my words weren't as scattered. I still just... didn't care about anything. It's been like that for most of it.
